records.notes: The aliens wanting to engage in the marching band practice, but being mad at a bad trumpeter is great. Finding ancient records of it is fine. "Intentionally playing poorly so they'll go away" (even though the aliens leave Earth bad reviews) is great. The lung-rupturing notes thing is weird. That can be cut. This can be a low-stakes case where the only problem is the aliens are being annoying and interrupting marching bandf practice.

I like the premise of people not remembering the people who lived here even though investigators find evidence of them. Putting together this weirdness and the lights and then finding out it's some weird supernatural creature is a fine case. The solution of reading names over the town's emergency speakers is kind of weird though. That's not a terrible solution, but I think it could be stronger. Townsfolk remembering their missing neighbors and their missing neighbor's debts is a fun sardonic ending. Can probably do more with that. The casserole thing is weak. I don't think that's needed.

Giant moths attracted to lights is a fine case but it's weird that the moths are attracted to their own eggs. If this is a big problem, how could the moths have been functioning so far. Maybe there's a story where townsfolk are think they're being menaced by monsters and the monsters are just big harmless (but annoying and scary) moths. Scared people turn on a bunch of lights in defense of the monsters, but skeptic people leave all their lights off and don't have any problems. So there's probably something in that. This isn't a "lights in the sky" story at all but it's a story that can probably be made to work.
